seoTitle: Dream Eater: Voice Dream Journal with Moon and Sky
metaDescription: Speak or type last night's dream, get a reading that asks instead of tells, and see the real moon beside it. The journal is free forever. For iPhone and iPad.
heroHeadline: Say the dream before it fades
heroSubhead: A voice-first dream journal for iPhone and iPad. Speak it or type it, keep it with the real moon and sky of that night, and ask for a reading that asks questions instead of handing you a verdict. The journal is free forever.
highlights: Voice capture that works offline, from the Lock Screen or Action Button
The real moon phase and sign stamped on every dream
Journal free forever, three free readings a week
Dreams stay on your iPhone, no account

features.title: Say it before it fades
features.body: Speak or type in seconds. Voice is turned into text on your iPhone and works offline, drafts survive a crash or a phone call, and a Bedside theme keeps the light low. Start recording from the Lock Screen, Control Center or the Action Button.

features.title: A reading that asks, not tells
features.body: It quotes your own words back, asks open questions and names the tradition when one reads an image a certain way: Jungian, Gestalt, folk. It never says a symbol has one fixed meaning and never predicts anything. Ask follow-up questions when you want to go further.

features.title: Painted from your words
features.body: Six art styles, from soft dreamscape to ink wash to collage, made from a short scene of the dream and never your raw text. Save the picture or share a card with the title and the moon.

features.title: The sky it happened under
features.body: Every dream is stamped with the moon phase and the Moon's sign, worked out on your iPhone, with a moon calendar and a moon widget for the Home and Lock Screen. Add birth details to see your chart. Astrology is optional and never a forecast.

features.title: Patterns that are honest
features.body: Your streak, tones and feelings, the themes that keep coming back and when you dream. Ask whether the moon matters and the app shows how many nights it takes to say anything, next to what chance alone would give you.

features.title: Private, and yours to take
features.body: Dreams, recordings, transcripts, tags and birth details stay on your iPhone. Lock the journal with Face ID or a passcode, export everything as Markdown and JSON, recover deletions for 30 days, or delete all data when you want it gone.

pricing.heading: The journal is free. Readings are optional.

pricing.footnote: US prices shown; your local price appears in the App Store. Subscriptions renew automatically until you cancel in your Apple Account settings. Prefer no subscription? Credit packs of 5, 15, 50 or 100 ($2.99, $7.99, $24.99, $39.99) never expire and pay for dream art and follow-up questions, one credit each.

faq.q: What is free and what costs money?
faq.a: The journal is free forever, including voice capture, search, export and App Lock, and every week includes three free readings. Plus adds unlimited readings, dream art, follow-up questions and your sky. The annual plan starts with a 7-day free trial, and Apple handles refunds and cancellations.

Dreams, recordings, transcripts, tags and birth details stay on your iPhone. A dream leaves the phone only when you ask for a reading, art or a follow-up. You can turn readings off, and Delete all data in Settings removes everything.

faq.q: Does it sync between my devices?
faq.a: Not in version 2.0. Dreams live on the device they were written on and are included in your device backup.

faq.q: What happens to the dreams I wrote in version 1?
faq.a: They move over automatically, along with your art, and a backup of the old data is kept for 30 days.

faq.q: Is this a medical or therapy tool?
faq.a: No. Dream Eater is for reflection and entertainment, and its readings offer perspectives rather than facts. If you are struggling, crisis resources are one tap away in Settings, under Help.

faq.q: Which devices and languages does it support?
faq.a: iPhone and iPad with iOS 26 or later, in English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese, and Simplified and Traditional Chinese.
